fragments.text: Despite the fact that AI invokes fear in many of us, it is also benefiting us in numerous ways. AI is revolutionizing the healthcare industry by providing a helping hand. Hello everyone, this is Dr. Puna Merotras, Senior Physotherapist, and I welcome you to this session on AI in healthcare. In this session, we would be understanding the different ways in which AI is impacting the healthcare industry. I would like to begin the session by understanding what exactly is AI and how it is transforming the world. We will also understand the history and benefits. And in the end, we will learn the future of AI in healthcare. AI sometimes called as machine intelligence is the intelligence demonstrated by machines

in contrast to the natural intelligence displayed by humans and animals. The term AI is used to describe machines that may make cognitive functions like humans associated with other human minds such as learning and complex problem solving. There are different types of artificial intelligence. Weak AI, the non-sentient machine intelligence typically focused on a narrow task. Strong AI or the artificial general intelligence are the machines with the ability to apply intelligence to any problem rather than just one specific problem, typically meaning at least as smart as typical human. Super intelligence, machines with artificial intelligence far surpassing that of the brightest and most gifted human minds. Due to recursive self improvement, super intelligence is expected to be a rapid outcome

of creating artificial general intelligence. AI can be used to solve real world problems by implementing the following processes or techniques like machine learning, natural language processing, expert systems, vision, speech, planning, and robotics. AI has already impacted the world and many industries have accepted AI and transforming themselves. Industries like manufacturing where it helps in reducing task time, medical tests and diagnosis where it helps in value added tasks that are performed such as reading an X-ray. In agriculture, it helps to identify macro-weather patterns that can impact harvest. In autonomous vehicle navigation, it helps in predicting accidents and continue to save lives. In healthcare delivery, it helps in analyzing X-rays and MRI images for accuracy and faster diagnosis.

In customer services like banking and financial services, it helps to deliver highly personalized customer service and also in the sector of education and carbon emission reduction. Now let's move on. And learn how artificial intelligence in healthcare is impacting. Since the origin of healthcare in 1950, it has impacted various domains, including finance, marketing, gaming industry and musical art. However, the biggest impact has been in the healthcare domain. The design of new AI systems have helped achieve medical advancements such as producing faster data collection and processing, assisting in more precise surgical procedures and more comprehensive implementation of electronic health records. AI has evolved and profoundly influenced the healthcare domain, especially in radiology, screening, psychiatry,

primary care, disease diagnosis and telemedicine. According to the studies by research Nestor, AI is set to grow at 45% CAGR for the next 10 years. Already the big players in the market like NVIDIA, Phillips, Siemens and Google are transforming themselves with AI. What is the reason behind the sudden growth of AI in healthcare? Let me narrow down for you. It is a significant decrement in the number of physicians. With the opportunities, there comes challenges and the biggest challenge is a lack of skilled workforce to develop AI. It is forecasted that by the year 2030, the market size of AI in healthcare is predicted to be $187 billion, which is currently $20 billion. Not only the big players in the market,

AI is also attracting a lot of startups. So these are the six top startups out of over thousands, which are disrupting the healthcare industry. Alone in year 2023, these 24 startups have already revolutionized the healthcare with AI. AI's role in healthcare can be divided into two ways. One is the clinical application and administrative applications. In clinical application, it helps in monitoring patients, supporting population health management, guiding surgical care, predicting health trajectories and recommending treatments. Whereas in administrative application, it helps in automating labor risk tasks regarding digital clinical notes and optimizing operational processes. AI has already transformed healthcare in various sectors like diagnostics, patient risk identification, supply chain management, virtual nursing assistance, fitness and nutrition and mental health.

Now let's look at India's approach to AI in healthcare industry. So AI technologies in healthcare started with radiology, particularly in treating TB. Gradually after the post-pandemic area, it has been widely used in other spheres like early detection and diagnosis of liver and lung issues, cancer, diabetes and also for various eye related issues. The National Center for Disease Control, along with the partnership with one private company, plans to create a database for the outbreak of almost 33 diseases. Needy IO has been actively involved in implementing AI in the early detection of diabetes. The government of India has also created a national digital health infrastructure to improvise digital health systems across the country, which includes health locker, personal health records,

digit doctors, coverage and claims digital platform, national health analytics platform and unique digital health ID for each citizen. This has not been an easy journey for implementing AI in healthcare. It has faced a lot of challenges like lack of broad-based expertise, lack of access to intelligent data, very high resource cost, lack of awareness for AI adoption and lastly lack of regulations on privacy. There has been an all-time high pressure on healthcare workers and we are on track to be shot of five million doctors by 2030. So this clearly shows how urgently AI is needed in healthcare to support our healthcare workers. There is no doubt that AI is expanding and evolving every day.

There are many potential applications like enhancing image scanning and segmentation, integration and improvement of workflow, disease risk prediction and supported decision making. Overall, the future of AI in healthcare looks promising. Thank you very much for listening.
